mainTopic: Closing פרק כל היד with the Tiberian cup, then the new משנה on a woman who passes tissue or odd shapes, and the גמרא's attempts to explain the argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן
overview: The גמרא finishes the rules for comparing blood to the color of 'diluted wine.' The standard is new, undiluted שרוני wine, and רב יצחק בר אבודימי says it must be looked at in a plain Tiberian cup, which אביי explains is thin enough for the color to show clearly. The פרק כל היד then ends with its הדרן. A new משנה opens the next פרק with a list of things a woman may pass. For a shapeless piece of tissue, the תנא קמא says she is טמאה only if blood came with it, while רבי יהודה says she is טמאה either way. Small pieces are tested in water, creature shapes need blood, and animal shapes count as a birth according to רבי מאיר, while the חכמים say only something with a human form is a ולד. In the גמרא, שמואל and רבי יוחנן each explain the argument through the color of the tissue. A ברייתא brought by רב הושעיא challenges both explanations, and attempts to save each one are rejected. רב נחמן בר יצחק then says the argument is really about whether the womb can open without blood. He starts linking this to an argument among תנאים, and that ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Sharon wine is judged like new, undiluted Carmelite wine
steps.stepSummary: The wine of the שרון, used to measure the color 'diluted wine,' is judged like כרמלי wine that is undiluted and new.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sharon wine is judged like Carmelite wine: undiluted, not diluted; new, not old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a statement it began earlier. It defines exactly which kind of wine sets the standard for the blood color called 'like diluted wine.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine colors differ by region, by whether water was added, and by age. This line fixes the standard: שרוני wine is treated like כרמלי wine that is pure (חי) and new (חדש). That gives the comparison one exact shade.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine from the Sharon region in ארץ ישראל
Literally 'alive'; undiluted wine with no water added

phrases.english: The Sharon wine is judged like Carmelite wine,
undiluted and not diluted,
new and not old.

steps.triggerLanguage: השרוני נידון ככרמלי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous page defining the blood color 'like diluted wine.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sharon wine, the measure for 'diluted wine' color, is judged like undiluted, new Carmelite wine.

steps.title: The comparison must be made in a plain Tiberian cup
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבודימי rules that all these wine-color comparisons are checked only in a simple Tiberian cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אבודימי said: And all of them are checked only in a plain Tiberian cup.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a practical rule about how the comparison is done. The wine used to compare the blood must be looked at in one specific kind of cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After fixing which wine sets the standard, the גמרא now fixes the vessel. The same wine can look darker or lighter depending on the cup, so the cup must be standardized too. The reason comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: We check or examine (here, comparing the blood's color)
A plain, simple cup made in טבריה

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Avudimi said:
And all of them, we do not check them
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the cases where blood is compared to the color of wine.

phrases.english: except with a plain Tiberian cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יצחק בר אבודימי וכולן אין בודקין אותן אלא בכוס טבריא פשוט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the required vessel for the wine-color comparison defined in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood is compared to wine only in a plain Tiberian cup.

steps.title: Why specifically a Tiberian cup?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב יצחק בר אבודימי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the cup has to come from טבריה. This question sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. The גמרא simply wants to understand the logic, since it is not obvious why one city's cup should matter for checking blood.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי טעמא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the comparison must use a plain Tiberian cup.

steps.title: אביי: the Tiberian cup is thinner, so the color shows better
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that normal cups are made thicker as they get bigger, but a Tiberian cup stays thin even when large, so the wine's redness is easier to see.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everywhere else in the world, a cup that holds one לוג is made from a מנה of material, and one that holds two לוגין is made from two hundred. A plain Tiberian cup, even one that holds two לוגין, is made from a מנה. And since it is thin, the color is more noticeable in it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. Tiberian cups are made very thin, so the wine's true color shows through clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary cups get more material as their size grows, so they stay thick. A Tiberian cup holding two לוגין uses only half the usual material, so its walls are thin and see-through. That lets the red of the wine be seen accurately, which matters when you compare it to blood.

keyTerms.meaning: A weight of one hundred (silver coins' worth)

steps.whatToRemember: The blood is compared to new, undiluted שרוני wine, looked at in a thin Tiberian cup where its true color shows clearly.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ מַחְזִיק לוֹג —
phrases.english: A cup of the whole world that holds a log —
they make it from a maneh,
phrases.notes: A מנה is a weight of a hundred coins; he means how much material goes into making the cup.

phrases.english: two logs — they make it from two hundred.
A plain Tiberian cup,
even if it holds two logs —
they make it from a maneh,
and since it is thin —
it is more noticeable in it.
phrases.notes: He means the wine's red color can be seen more clearly through the thin cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי של כל העולם כולו מחזיק לוג עושין אותו ממנה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Tiberian cup is made with half the usual material, so it is thin and the wine's color shows more clearly.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter כל היד
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter כל היד.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, כל היד.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter כל היד. The next line starts a new chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional closing that expresses the hope to come back and learn the chapter again. It is not a legal statement.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)
The name of the chapter that just ended

phrases.english: We will return to you, Kol HaYad.

steps.triggerLanguage: הדרן עלך כל היד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion of steps 1-4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter כל היד is complete.

steps.title: A woman who passes a piece of tissue: impure only with blood, or always?
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a woman who passes a shapeless piece of tissue is טמאה if blood came with it and טהורה if not. רבי יהודה says she is טמאה either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman who passes a piece of tissue: if there is blood with it, she is impure; and if not, she is pure. רבי יהודה says: Either way, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה about a woman who passes a shapeless piece of flesh. The תנא קמא and רבי יהודה disagree about whether she is טמאה when no blood is seen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the piece of tissue alone does not make her טמאה. Only blood that comes out with it does. רבי יהודה rules she is טמאה even when no blood is seen, and the משנה does not give his reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who passes or miscarries something
A piece (here, a shapeless piece of tissue)

steps.confusionAlert: The two sides do not argue when blood is seen; everyone agrees she is טמאה then. The disagreement is only when no blood is seen with the tissue.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the new chapter's main topic: which things passed by a woman make her טמאה. It sets up the מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Mishnah: A woman who passes a piece,
phrases.notes: The 'piece' is a shapeless piece of flesh, not a formed fetus.

phrases.english: if there is blood with it — she is impure,
and if not — she is pure.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
either way — she is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתני' המפלת חתיכה אם יש עמה דם טמאה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן of step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: a woman who passes a piece of tissue is טמאה only if blood came with it. רבי יהודה: she is טמאה either way.

steps.title: Tiny discharges are tested in water
steps.stepSummary: If a woman discharges something like a shell, a hair, dirt or red gnats, she puts it in water. If it dissolves she is טמאה, and if not she is טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who discharges something that looks like a shell, a hair, dirt, or red gnats should put it in water. If it dissolves, she is impure. If not, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of strange discharges and gives a simple test for small, odd-looking pieces: put them in water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These small things might really be dried, clumped blood. Water tells us. If the piece melts away, it was blood and she is טמאה as a נדה. If it stays solid, it is not blood and she is טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: She should put it into water (to test it)

phrases.english: A woman who discharges something like a shell,
like a hair, like dirt,
like red gnats —
she should put it into water:
if they dissolve, she is impure,
and if not, she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפֶּלֶת כְּמִין קְלִיפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of discharges begun in step 6 (the shapeless piece of tissue).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Small discharges that look like a shell, hair, dirt or red gnats are tested in water. If they dissolve she is טמאה, and if not she is טהורה.

steps.title: Creature-shaped discharges need blood to make her impure
steps.stepSummary: If she discharges something shaped like fish, grasshoppers, שקצים or רמשים, she is טמאה only if blood came out with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who discharges something like fish, grasshoppers, repulsive creatures, or creeping creatures is impure if blood comes with them. If not, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new group: discharges shaped like small creatures. Here there is no water test. The only question is whether blood came out with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These shapes are solid tissue and do not count as a birth. So the piece itself does not make her טמאה. Only blood that comes out with it does, just like the rule for the shapeless piece in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Creeping creatures that crawl on the ground

phrases.english: A woman who discharges something like fish,
grasshoppers, repulsive creatures, or creeping creatures —
if there is blood with them, she is impure,
and if not, she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפֶּלֶת כְּמִין דָּגִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case in the משנה's list. It uses a blood test instead of the water test of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Discharges shaped like fish, grasshoppers, שקצים or רמשים make her טמאה only if blood came with them.

steps.title: Animal-shaped discharges count as a birth of a male or female
steps.stepSummary: If she discharges something shaped like a בהמה, חיה or bird, kosher or not, she keeps the birth days for a male if it is male and for a female if it is female.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who discharges the form of a domestic animal, wild animal, or bird, whether a kosher or non-kosher kind: if it is male, she keeps the days for a male birth. If it is female, she keeps the days for a female birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a bigger case: a discharge shaped like an animal or bird. This opinion treats it like a real birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes further than steps 7-8. Here the discharge itself is treated as a child, so she keeps the Torah's days after birth, which are different for a boy and a girl. Step 10 will tell us this is the view of רבי מאיר, and the חכמים disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: A domestic animal (like a cow or sheep)
Here: non-kosher / kosher species of animals
Literally 'she sits': she keeps the set days of impurity and purity after a birth

steps.confusionAlert: Here טמאין and טהורין mean non-kosher and kosher kinds of animals. They are not talking about the woman's purity.

phrases.english: A woman who discharges the form of a domestic animal,
a wild animal, or a bird,
whether non-kosher kinds or kosher kinds —
if it is male, she keeps the days for a male,
and if it is female, she keeps the days for a female.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפֶּלֶת מִין בְּהֵמָה, חַיָּה וָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from discharges that matter only because of blood (steps 7-8) to a discharge treated as an actual birth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A discharge in the form of an animal or bird is treated as a birth. She keeps the days for a male or a female according to its gender.

steps.title: Unknown gender, and the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: If the gender is unknown, רבי מאיר says she keeps the stricter rules of both a male and a female birth. The חכמים say anything without a human form is not a ולד at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is not known whether it was male or female, she keeps the days for both a male and a female. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: anything that has no human form is not a baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the animal-shape case and reveals that the whole ruling is רבי מאיר's. Then the חכמים give their opposing view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When we cannot tell the gender, רבי מאיר makes her follow whichever rule is stricter from each side: a male birth or a female birth. The חכמים say the birth rules apply only when the discharge has some human form. So an animal shape does not count as a birth, and she is not treated as a woman who gave birth.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not known (we can't tell if it was male or female)
A baby, offspring (something that counts as a birth)

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'the words of רבי מאיר' cover the whole animal-shape ruling in step 9, not just the unknown-gender line. The חכמים disagree with all of it.
steps.whatToRemember: For animal or bird shapes, רבי מאיר says it counts as a birth (male, female, or both if unknown). The חכמים say only something with a human form counts as a ולד.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of the חכמים, that a ולד needs צורת אדם, becomes the key test for when a miscarriage brings the laws of a woman who gave birth.

phrases.english: And if it is not known —
she keeps the days for a male and for a female,
phrases.notes: She follows the stricter side of each: the longer impure days of a girl, and only the shorter pure days of a boy.

phrases.english: these are the words of רבי מאיר.
And the Sages say:
anything that has no human form
is not a baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אֵין יָדוּעַ — תֵּשֵׁב לְזָכָר וְלַנְּקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 9's case with the unknown-gender rule. It names רבי מאיר as the author and adds the dissent of the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: if the gender is unknown, she keeps the rules of both a male and a female birth. חכמים: anything without a human form is not a ולד.

steps.title: שמואל limits רבי יהודה to tissue with impure-blood coloring
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says רבי יהודה calls the woman טמאה only if the tissue has the color of one of the ארבעת מיני דמים. Any other color is טהורה even according to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי יהודה called her טמאה only when the piece of tissue has the color of one of the four kinds of impure blood. But if it has the color of other kinds of blood, she is טהורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining the משנה's argument. שמואל narrows רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה said she is טמאה 'either way', even with no blood. שמואל says that 'either way' covers only tissue whose color matches impure blood. If the tissue is some other color, רבי יהודה agrees she is טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The four kinds (colors) of blood that make a woman טמאה
Other kinds of blood, colors that do not make her טמאה
A piece of tissue, a shapeless lump

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ' אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
phrases.notes: Don't mix up the two. רב יהודה is the אמורא quoting שמואל. רבי יהודה is the תנא from the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda declared her impure only
with a piece of tissue having the color of the four kinds of blood,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שֶׁל שְׁאָר מִינֵי דָמִים — טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.english: but if it has the color of other kinds of blood, she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לֹא טִימֵּא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's explanation of the משנה in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה calls her טמאה only for tissue with impure-blood coloring. With any other color she is טהורה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: when the color is known, everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן offers a different reading. If the tissue's color is known, there is no argument at all: impure-blood color means טמאה, and any other color means טהורה, for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: If the tissue has the color of one of the four kinds of blood, everyone agrees she is טמאה. If it has the color of other kinds of blood, everyone agrees she is טהורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second explanation of the משנה. He says that in the cases where the color is known, there is no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל held that the argument is about impure-colored tissue that came without blood. רבי יוחנן says even the רבנן agree that impure-colored tissue makes her טמאה. This step clears away the known-color cases and sets up where the real argument lies (next step).

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees; it is the opinion of all

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל אַרְבַּעַת מִינֵי דָמִים — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: if it is of the four kinds of blood, everyone agrees she is impure;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל שְׁאָר מִינֵי דָמִים — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.english: if it is of other kinds of blood, everyone agrees she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative to שמואל's reading in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the tissue's color is known, there is no argument. Impure color means טמאה and other colors mean טהורה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the argument is only when she doesn't know what the tissue looked like
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן, the argument is only when the woman does not know what she passed. רבי יהודה follows the majority, since most tissue has impure-blood coloring. The רבנן do not accept that majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue only where she passed tissue and does not know what she passed. רבי יהודה holds: follow the majority of pieces of tissue, and most pieces of tissue have the color of the four kinds of blood. And the רבנן hold: we do not say that most pieces of tissue have the color of the four kinds of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes his explanation by pinpointing the one case where they argue, and the reason each side holds its view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument shifts from a question about color to a question about a majority (רוב). רבי יהודה says most such tissue has impure coloring, so we assume this one did too, and she is טמאה. The רבנן do not accept that majority, so she stays טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Go after the majority; decide based on what usually happens
We do not say (we do not accept this reasoning)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: the argument is about impure-colored tissue that came without blood. רבי יוחנן: when the color is known, everyone agrees; the argument is only when the color is unknown, and it depends on רוב.

phrases.english: They disagree only where she discharged tissue
and she does not know what she discharged.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: זִיל בָּתַר רוֹב חֲתִיכוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds: Go after the majority of pieces of tissue,

phrases.aramaic: וְרוֹב חֲתִיכוֹת שֶׁל (מִינֵי) אַרְבַּעַת מִינֵי דָמִים הָוְיָין.
phrases.english: and most pieces of tissue are of the four kinds of blood.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. It just repeats 'kinds', so the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold: We do not say

phrases.aramaic: רוֹב חֲתִיכוֹת שֶׁל אַרְבַּעַת מִינֵי דָמִים.
phrases.english: that most pieces of tissue are of the four kinds of blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁהִפִּילָה, וְאֵינָהּ יוֹדַעַת מָה הִפִּילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's statement from Step 12 by naming the case they argue about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They argue only when the color is unknown. רבי יהודה relies on רוב to say she is טמאה; the רבנן do not.

steps.title: רב הושעיא's ברייתא lists four colors and still records the argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges both readings with a ברייתא. It speaks of tissue that is red, black, green or white, so the color is known and includes non-impure colors. It still says the רבנן rule טהורה without blood and רבי יהודה rules טמאה either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But when רב הושעיא came from נהרדעא, he brought a ברייתא with him: A woman who passes a piece of tissue that is red, black, green or white: if blood comes with it, she is טמאה; if not, she is טהורה. רבי יהודה says: either way she is טמאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks 'Is that so?' and brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict both שמואל and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives known colors, including green and white, which are not impure-blood colors. Even so, it says the רבנן rule טהורה without blood and רבי יהודה rules טמאה either way. That clashes with both explanations above.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? This opens a challenge.
A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא,
phrases.english: But when Rav Hoshaya came from Neharde'a,
he came and brought a baraita in his hand:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּפֶּלֶת חֲתִיכָה אֲדוּמָּה, שְׁחוֹרָה, יְרוּקָּה, וּלְבָנָה —
phrases.english: A woman who discharges a piece of tissue that is red, black, green, or white:
if there is blood with it, she is impure;
and if not, she is pure.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ טְמֵאָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Either way she is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks both explanations given in Steps 11 to 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading (Step 11) and רבי יוחנן's reading (Steps 12 and 13)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא records the argument even for known colors, including non-impure colors like green and white. That contradicts both of the narrower readings.

steps.title: One difficulty for שמואל, two for רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up the damage: the ברייתא makes one problem for שמואל and two problems for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a difficulty for שמואל in one point, and for רבי יוחנן in two points.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא counts how many problems the ברייתא causes for each אמורא. This sets up the detailed explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל: he said רבי יהודה calls her טמאה only with impure-blood colors, but the ברייתא has him ruling טמאה even for green and white. For רבי יוחנן there are two problems. The רבנן say טהורה even for red and black, which he said everyone agrees is טמאה. And רבי יהודה says טמאה even for green and white, which he said everyone agrees is טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty, a problem with a view

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think שמואל and רבי יוחנן are hit by the same problem. שמואל already agreed there is an argument when no blood comes with the tissue. Only his limit to impure colors is challenged. רבי יוחנן said there is no argument at all for known colors, so he is hit from both directions.

phrases.english: It is difficult for Shmuel in one point,
and for Rabbi Yoḥanan in two points.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל בַּחֲדָא, וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּתַרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out how the ברייתא in Step 14 hurts each of the two readings.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל (one point) and רבי יוחנן (two points)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's limit of רבי יהודה's ruling to impure colors is contradicted. Both of רבי יוחנן's 'everyone agrees' claims are contradicted by the recorded argument over known colors.

steps.title: The one problem for שמואל
steps.stepSummary: שמואל said רבי יהודה rules טמאה only for tissue with an impure-blood color. Yet the ברייתא lists green and white tissue and still has רבי יהודה disagreeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is the one problem for שמואל. שמואל said רבי יהודה calls her impure only when the tissue has one of the four impure-blood colors. But the ברייתא mentions green and white, and רבי יהודה still disagrees!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens the detailed explanation of step 15 by showing exactly how the ברייתא contradicts שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Green and white are not impure-blood colors, so according to שמואל רבי יהודה should agree she is טהורה. But the ברייתא includes green and white in the list where רבי יהודה rules טמאה either way. That clashes directly with שמואל's limit.

keyTerms.meaning: A piece of tissue the woman passed
The four colors of blood that make a woman impure
Green and white, colors that are not impure blood

phrases.english: For שמואל, there is one problem:
phrases.notes: This picks up step 15, where the ברייתא was one problem for שמואל and two for רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: for שמואל said:
Rabbi Yehuda did not declare her impure

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בַּחֲתִיכָה שֶׁל אַרְבַּעַת מִינֵי דָמִים,
phrases.english: except with tissue of the four kinds of blood,
but look, the ברייתא teaches 'green and white,'
and Rabbi Yehuda disagrees!
phrases.notes: He means רבי יהודה still says טמאה for those colors, which שמואל said he would not.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִשְׁמוּאֵל בַּחֲדָא, דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'one problem for שמואל' announced in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that רבי יהודה rules טמאה only for impure-blood colors (step 11)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists green and white, which are not impure colors, and still has רבי יהודה ruling טמאה.

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי יהודה only argues about red and black
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a way to save שמואל: perhaps in the ברייתא רבי יהודה disagrees only about the red and black tissue, and agrees about green and white.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: when רבי יהודה disagrees, it is only about red and black tissue, but about green and white he does not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible defense of שמואל. This is a setup, because the next step will knock it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Red and black are impure-blood colors, so arguing about them fits שמואל. The idea is to split the ברייתא's list: רבי יהודה's 'טמאה either way' would cover only the red and black cases. If that works, the ברייתא no longer contradicts שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say, introducing a possible answer
Red and black, colors among the impure bloods

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggestion. The גמרא does not accept it; the next step shows why it fails.

phrases.english: And if you would say,
when Rabbi Yehuda disagrees,
it is about red and black,
but about green and white, he does not,
phrases.notes: So for green and white, רבי יהודה would agree with the רבנן that she is טהורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא, כִּי פְּלִיג רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַאֲדוּמָּה וּשְׁחוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a reading of the ברייתא to escape the problem in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רבי יהודה's ruling in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seems to have רבי יהודה ruling טמאה for every color listed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps רבי יהודה's disagreement covers only red and black, matching שמואל.

steps.title: Then why mention green and white at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. If רבי יהודה agrees about green and white, those colors would be listed for no reason, since the רבנן already call red and black טהורה. So green and white must be there to show רבי יהודה disagrees about them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, for whose sake does the ברייתא teach green and white? If for the רבנן: now that the רבנן call red and black pure, do we even need to say green and white are pure? Rather, it must be for רבי יהודה, to show that he disagrees!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from step 17, so the problem for שמואל stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן rule טהורה even for red and black, which look like impure blood, so green and white are obviously טהורה for them. Mentioning green and white would teach nothing new about the רבנן. The only reason to list them is that רבי יהודה rules טמאה even there, and that contradicts שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: For whom does it teach it? Whose view is this detail meant to show?
Now that the bigger case is so, is the smaller case even a question?

steps.whatToRemember: A ברייתא does not list a case for nothing. Green and white must be there to show רבי יהודה rules טמאה even for them, so the ברייתא really does contradict שמואל.

phrases.english: But then green and white,
for whose sake does it teach them?
If you say for the רבנן,
now that red and black
the רבנן declare pure,
do green and white even need to be said?
Rather, is it not for Rabbi Yehuda,
and he disagrees!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יְרוּקָּה וּלְבָנָה לְמַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the defense proposed in step 17, so step 16's challenge against שמואל stands.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that רבי יהודה argues only about red and black.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under that reading, listing green and white would be pointless, since the רבנן obviously call them טהורה.

steps.title: The extra problem for רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן said that with an impure-blood color everyone agrees she is טמאה. Yet the ברייתא lists red and black tissue and has the רבנן disagreeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, there is a problem for רבי יוחנן, who said: if the tissue has one of the four impure-blood colors, everyone agrees she is impure. But the ברייתא teaches red and black, and the רבנן disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows the second problem for רבי יוחנן, on top of the first one he shares with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's first problem matches שמואל's: he also said green and white are טהורה for everyone, yet רבי יהודה rules טמאה. His second problem goes the other way. Red and black are impure-blood colors, so the רבנן should agree she is טמאה, but the ברייתא has them ruling טהורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why step 15 said 'two problems' for רבי יוחנן: the ברייתא contradicts him about both the non-impure colors and the impure colors.

phrases.english: And furthermore, for Rabbi Yochanan, who said:
tissue of the four kinds of blood,
everyone agrees she is impure,
but the ברייתא teaches red and black,
and the רבנן disagree!
phrases.notes: The רבנן call her טהורה when there is no blood, even for these impure-blood colors.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing שמואל's problem, the גמרא turns to the additional problem for רבי יוחנן announced in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that with an impure-blood color everyone agrees she is טמאה (step 12)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists red and black, which are impure colors, and still has the רבנן ruling טהורה.

steps.title: A suggestion to save רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the רבנן argue only about green and white tissue, and agree that red and black tissue makes her טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: the רבנן argue only about green and white, but about red and black they do not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a way to protect רבי יוחנן from the question in Step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that when the tissue has an impure-blood color, everyone agrees she is טמאה. This suggestion reads the ברייתא so that the רבנן disagree only about green and white. That way red and black would stay as cases where everyone says טמאה, just as רבי יוחנן said.

phrases.english: And if you will say,
the רבנן argue only about green and white,
but about red and black, no.
phrases.notes: He means that on red and black the רבנן agree with רבי יהודה that she is טמאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, כִּי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן אַיְּרוּקָּה וּלְבָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 19, the same way Step 17 tried to answer the question against שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the argument in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows the רבנן arguing about red and black tissue, which goes against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read the רבנן as arguing only about green and white, so red and black are טמאה according to everyone.

steps.title: Red and black must be teaching the רבנן's view
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה calls even green and white טמאה, listing red and black for him would be pointless. So red and black must be listed to teach the רבנן's view, and the רבנן argue about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, for whose sake does the ברייתא teach red and black? If you say for רבי יהודה: now that green and white are טמאה in his view, do we even need to say red and black are? Rather, isn't it for the רבנן, which shows that they argue?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from Step 20 using a logic test: every case in the ברייתא has to teach something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה calls even non-blood colors like green and white טמאה, so it is obvious that he would call red and black טמאה too. That means the red and black cases cannot be there for him. They must be there to show the רבנן's view, and that view is that she is טהורה. So the רבנן do argue about red and black, and the question against רבי יוחנן stands.

keyTerms.meaning: for whose view is it taught?
now that (the bigger case is true), is (the smaller case) even needed?
rather, isn't it...? (introduces the only remaining option)

steps.confusionAlert: This is the mirror image of Step 18. There, green and white had to be teaching רבי יהודה's view. Here, red and black have to be teaching the רבנן's view.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲדוּמָּה וּשְׁחוֹרָה לְמַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ?
phrases.english: But red and black, for whom does it teach them?
If you say for רבי יהודה,
now that green and white are טמאה,
is it even necessary to say red and black?
Rather, isn't it for the רבנן, and they argue!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֲדוּמָּה וּשְׁחוֹרָה לְמַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer offered in Step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that the רבנן agree about red and black
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the red and black cases in the ברייתא pointless, because for רבי יהודה they are obvious.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the argument is about whether the womb can open without blood
steps.stepSummary: The argument is not about colors at all. It is about whether the womb can open without any blood coming out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: they argue about whether the womb can open without blood.
steps.whatsHappening: Both explanations based on color have run into trouble, so רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a completely new reason for the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, שמואל and רבי יוחנן tied the argument to the color of the tissue. רב נחמן בר יצחק says the real question is something else. רבי יהודה holds that the womb cannot open without blood, so she is טמאה whatever the color. The רבנן hold that it can open without blood, so she is טהורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the whole argument away from the color of the tissue and onto a basic question about how the body works. That is why the colors listed in the ברייתא no longer cause a problem.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
About whether it is possible for the womb to open
phrases.notes: Literally "the grave." Here it is a way of saying the womb.

phrases.english: without blood, they argue,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the color-based explanations were questioned (Steps 15 to 21), a new explanation replaces them.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the argument is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן depends on the color of the tissue.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument depends on whether the womb can open without blood, whatever the color.

steps.title: Linking the argument to a disagreement of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says this question is the same one that תנאים argue about, and the גמרא starts quoting their ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they argue about the same point that these תנאים argue about, as it is taught: if she had hard labor for two days, and on the third day she miscarried, and she does not know what she miscarried...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that shows the same question about the womb opening without blood, and the quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק backs up his new explanation by showing that other תנאים also argue about whether the womb can open without blood. The case in this ברייתא is a woman who had hard labor for two days, then miscarried on the third day without knowing what came out. The argument itself will come in the rest of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים, the sages of the משנה era

phrases.english: And it is the same argument as these תנאים have,
as it is taught: she had hard labor for two days,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is assuming she saw blood on those two days.

phrases.english: and on the third day she miscarried,
and she does not know what she miscarried,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִפְלוּגְתָּא דְהָנֵי תַנָּאֵי, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's new explanation by linking it to an earlier disagreement among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That whether the womb can open without blood is a real question that תנאים argue about
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a woman who had hard labor for two days and miscarried on the third
